# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lang_2023_cholecalciferol"))$reference`
* Final model (VDORA Parts 1 and 2): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lang_2023_cholecalciferol"))$description`
* Interim model (VDORA Part 1): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lang_2023_cholecalciferol_part1"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-023-01285-9> (open access; PMC10582143)
* Electronic Supplementary Material (ESM): covariate-model building tables (ESM Tables 1 and 3), prediction-error summary (ESM Table 2) and model diagnostics, available from the article page.

The VDORA study gave oral vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) for 16 weeks to
children with asthma and overweight or obesity and followed serum
25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) for a further 12 weeks. The paper reports two
population PK models, both packaged here:

* `Lang_2023_cholecalciferol_part1` -- the interim model fitted to the 44
  children of Part 1 (Table 2). It has no covariates and was used to simulate
  candidate regimens (Table 3, Figures 2 and 3) and pick the Part 2 regimen
  (50,000 IU loading dose + 8000 IU daily).
* `Lang_2023_cholecalciferol` -- the final model refitted to Parts 1 and 2
  combined (Table 4, Eqs 7-9), with the BMI-for-age z-score scaling clearance,
  central volume and intercompartmental clearance.

Both models describe 25(OH)D, not vitamin D3 itself: the vitamin D3 dose is
absorbed (first order, very slowly: Ka about 0.002 1/h, an absorption
half-life near two weeks) directly into a two-compartment 25(OH)D
disposition model, and a constant endogenous input keeps the untreated
concentration at the estimated baseline BASE.

## Units

The models work in molar units: doses in nmol of vitamin D3 and
concentrations in nmol/L of 25(OH)D (BASE is reported in nmol/L). The paper
reports doses in international units and its targets in ng/mL, so the
vignette converts with

* 1 IU vitamin D3 = 0.025 ug; molecular weight 384.64 g/mol, so
  1 IU = 0.0650 nmol (50,000 IU = 3250 nmol; 8000 IU = 520 nmol);
* 25(OH)D3 molecular weight 400.64 g/mol, so 1 ng/mL = 2.496 nmol/L
  (40 ng/mL = 99.8 nmol/L).

```{r units}
iu_to_nmol <- 0.025 * 1000 / 384.64 # nmol vitamin D3 per IU
nmolL_per_ngmL <- 1000 / 400.64 # nmol/L 25(OH)D per ng/mL
```

The paper does not state the dose unit used in the NONMEM data set. Dosing
in nmol reproduces the published regimen simulations of Table 3 (below);
dosing in ug would put the typical week-16 concentration on 50,000 IU +
8000 IU daily near 34 ng/mL, against the 82% of simulated children above
40 ng/mL that Table 3 reports, so the molar reading is the one consistent
with the paper.

# Population

The VDORA study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03686150) enrolled children aged 6-17
years with physician-diagnosed asthma, BMI at or above the 85th percentile
for age and sex, and baseline serum 25(OH)D of 10 to < 30 ng/mL (Methods).
Part 1 randomised 44 children (Table 1 cohorts A-D: 50,000 IU loading +
6000 IU daily, 50,000 IU loading + 10,000 IU daily, 6000 IU daily, 600 IU
daily) and contributed 227 concentrations; Part 2 randomised 63 children 2:1
to 50,000 IU loading + 8000 IU daily (cohort E) or 600 IU daily (cohort F).
The combined model used 848 concentrations from 109 children. Across the
tabulated cohorts, median ages were 11.2-13.4 years, 48.6% were female,
41% White and 41% Black, 18% Hispanic, and 23 / 35 / 49 children were
overweight / obese / morbidly obese (85th-95th / 95th-99th / >= 99th BMI
percentile). Median baseline 25(OH)D was 14.5-21 ng/mL.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Lang_2023_cholecalciferol")()$population, give.attr = FALSE)
```

# Source trace

|---|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment, first-order absorption, linear elimination | -- | -- | Results "Part 1 PK Model Development"; Methods "Combined Model Development" |
| Constant endogenous input; baseline BASE | `kin = CL/F * BASE` | same | Results ("A constant endogenous input rate to the central compartment ... A parameter (BASE) was used to describe the baseline") |
| `lka` (Ka, 1/h) | 0.0022 | 0.00178 | Table 4 / Table 2 |
| `lcl` (CL/F, L/h) | 0.179 | 0.0858 | Table 4 / Table 2 |
| `lvc` (Vc/F, L) | 30.2 | 35.2 | Table 4 / Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q/F, L/h) | 0.116 | 0.189 | Table 4 / Table 2 |

| BMIZ reference | 2.36 | -- | Eqs 7-9 (cohort median z-score) |

# Part 1 model: regimen simulations

## Virtual cohort and simulation

Part 1 simulated six regimens for 16 weeks in the 44 Part 1 children using
their individual empirical Bayes estimates (Table 3, Figure 2), and two of
them for 52 weeks (Figure 3). The individual estimates are not published,
so the vignette draws 200 virtual children per regimen from the Part 1
model's population distribution instead.

```{r part1-events}
make_regimen <- function(n, ld_iu, md_iu, dose_weeks, obs_weeks, regimen,
                         id_offset = 0L, BMIZ = NULL) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  daily <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = md_iu * iu_to_nmol, ii = 24,
    addl = dose_weeks * 7 - 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  loading <- if (ld_iu > 0) {
    tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = ld_iu * iu_to_nmol, ii = 0, addl = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  }
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_weeks * 7 * 24) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, ii = 0, addl = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ev <- bind_rows(loading, daily, obs) |>
    mutate(regimen = regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  if (!is.null(BMIZ)) {
    ev <- left_join(ev, tibble(id = ids, BMIZ = BMIZ), by = "id")
  }
  ev
}

regimens_p1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~ld_iu, ~md_iu, ~pct40, ~pct100, ~pct150,
  "1: 50,000 IU LD + 10,000 IU/day", 50000, 10000, 98, 7, 0,
  "2: 50,000 IU LD + 9000 IU/day", 50000, 9000, 93, 2, 0,
  "3: 50,000 IU LD + 8000 IU/day", 50000, 8000, 82, 0, 0,
  "4: 50,000 IU LD + 5000 IU/day", 50000, 5000, 66, 0, 0,
  "5: 8000 IU/day", 0, 8000, 82, 0, 0,
  "6: 600 IU/day", 0, 600, 0, 0, 0
)

n_per_arm <- 200
events_p1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens_p1)), function(i) {
  make_regimen(
    n_per_arm, regimens_p1$ld_iu[i], regimens_p1$md_iu[i],
    dose_weeks = 16, obs_weeks = 0:52, regimen = regimens_p1$regimen[i],
    id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm
  )
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_p1[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt")])))

mod_p1 <- readModelDb("Lang_2023_cholecalciferol_part1")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)
sim_p1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_p1, events = events_p1, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(week = time / (7 * 24), conc_ngmL = Cc / nmolL_per_ngmL)
```

## Table 3: target attainment at week 16

```{r part1-table3}
tab3 <- sim_p1 |>
  filter(week == 16) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    sim40 = 100 * mean(conc_ngmL >= 40),
    sim100 = 100 * mean(conc_ngmL >= 100),
    sim150 = 100 * mean(conc_ngmL >= 150),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(regimens_p1, by = "regimen")

tab3 |>
  select(regimen, pct40, sim40, pct100, sim100, pct150, sim150) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    ">= 40 ng/mL, published (%)" = pct40,
    ">= 40 ng/mL, simulated (%)" = sim40,
    ">= 100 ng/mL, published (%)" = pct100,
    ">= 100 ng/mL, simulated (%)" = sim100,
    ">= 150 ng/mL, published (%)" = pct150,
    ">= 150 ng/mL, simulated (%)" = sim150
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Lang 2023 (Part 1 model, 16 weeks of treatment).")

stopifnot(
  # The 40 ng/mL attainment depends on the dose (unit), CL/F and BASE together;
  # dosing in ug instead of nmol moves regimen 3 from about 82% to about 25%.
  # Observed while authoring: per-regimen differences of 0-6 points, which
  # are the gap between the population distribution sampled here and the
  # 44 shrunk individual estimates the paper simulated.
  median(abs(tab3$sim40 - tab3$pct40)) < 10,
  max(abs(tab3$sim40 - tab3$pct40)) < 20,
  # The paper's standard-of-care arm never reaches 40 ng/mL.
  tab3$sim40[tab3$md_iu == 600] < 5
)
```

The simulated attainment agrees with Table 3 to within a few percentage
points for every regimen. The published percentages come from the 44 Part 1
children's empirical Bayes estimates, whose spread is shrunk relative to the
model's population distribution, so the simulated tails (regimen 1's
attainment, the small fraction above 100 ng/mL) are slightly wider than
published.


# Final model (Parts 1 and 2)

## Virtual cohort

The BMI z-score distribution is not tabulated. The virtual cohort draws a
z-score for each child from a normal distribution centred on the reported
median of 2.36 (SD 0.6), truncated to 1.04-3.8: 1.04 is the z-score of the
85th percentile (the enrolment criterion) and 3.8 is a plausible upper end
for severe paediatric obesity.

```{r final-events}
draw_bmiz <- function(n) {
  z <- numeric(0)
  while (length(z) < n) {
    x <- rnorm(n, 2.36, 0.6)
    z <- c(z, x[x >= 1.04 & x <= 3.8])
  }
  z[seq_len(n)]
}
set.seed(109)
events_p2 <- bind_rows(
  make_regimen(n_per_arm, 50000, 8000, 16, c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28),
    "E: 50,000 IU LD + 8000 IU/day", 0L,
    BMIZ = draw_bmiz(n_per_arm)
  ),
  make_regimen(n_per_arm, 0, 600, 16, c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28),
    "F: 600 IU/day", n_per_arm,
    BMIZ = draw_bmiz(n_per_arm)
  )
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_p2[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt")])))

mod <- readModelDb("Lang_2023_cholecalciferol")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
sim_p2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_p2, keep = c("regimen", "BMIZ")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(week = time / (7 * 24), conc_ngmL = Cc / nmolL_per_ngmL)
```

```{r final-figure4}
  )
```

## Part 2 target attainment at week 16

The Discussion reports that 79% of children on 50,000 IU + 8000 IU daily
reached 40 ng/mL at week 16, none on 600 IU daily did, and 6% of those on the
loading regimen exceeded 100 ng/mL.

```{r final-attainment}
att_p2 <- sim_p2 |>
  filter(week == 16) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    sim40 = 100 * mean(conc_ngmL >= 40),
    sim100 = 100 * mean(conc_ngmL > 100),
    median_ngmL = median(conc_ngmL),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(obs40 = c(79, 0), obs100 = c(6, 0))

att_p2 |>
  select(regimen, obs40, sim40, obs100, sim100, median_ngmL) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    ">= 40 ng/mL, observed (%)" = obs40,
    ">= 40 ng/mL, simulated (%)" = sim40,
    "> 100 ng/mL, observed (%)" = obs100,
    "> 100 ng/mL, simulated (%)" = sim100,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = median_ngmL
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Week-16 attainment in Part 2: observed (Discussion) vs simulated (final model).")

stopifnot(
  abs(att_p2$sim40[1] - 79) < 15,
  att_p2$sim40[2] < 5
)
```

The simulated attainment of 40 ng/mL on the loading regimen sits a few
points above the observed 79%, and the simulated fraction above 100 ng/mL is
somewhat above the observed 6%. The observed percentages come from the 43
children of cohort E, and the virtual cohort's BMI z-score distribution is
assumed (see Virtual cohort), so differences of this size are expected.

## Table 5: concentrations by BMI z-score group

Table 5 tabulates week-16 predictions on 50,000 IU + 8000 IU daily by
BMI z-score group. The typical-value curves below (no between-subject
variability, BASE = 42.6 nmol/L) show the direction of the covariate
effect: a higher z-score raises clearance and shortens the half-life, so
both the rise during treatment and the post-treatment fall are faster.

```{r final-typical}
typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(1.5, 2.36, 3.4)), function(i) {
  z <- c(1.5, 2.36, 3.4)[i]
  make_regimen(1, 50000, 8000, 16, seq(0, 52, by = 0.5),
    sprintf("BMIZ %.2f", z), i - 1L,
    BMIZ = z
  )
}))
# Three typical subjects that differ only in BMIZ; rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
sim_typ <- suppressWarnings(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events, keep = c("regimen", "BMIZ"))
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(week = time / (7 * 24), conc_ngmL = Cc / nmolL_per_ngmL)

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(week, conc_ngmL, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 40, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Serum 25(OH)D (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value profiles, 50,000 IU loading + 8000 IU daily for 16 weeks."
  )

sim_typ |>
  filter(week == 16) |>
  select(regimen, conc_ngmL) |>
  mutate(published_median_group = c(51, 49, 31)) |>
  rename(
    "BMI z-score" = regimen,
    "Typical week-16 concentration (ng/mL)" = conc_ngmL,
    "Table 5 population-predicted median of the group (ng/mL)" = published_median_group
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The typical-value concentrations fall with the z-score as in Table 5, but are
higher than the Table 5 group medians (by about 20 ng/mL in the morbidly obese
group). Table 5's population predictions span 10-110 ng/mL within groups whose
typical values differ by only a few ng/mL, so the tabulated predictions were
not computed from the typical parameters alone; the table is reproduced here
for orientation and not used as a gate.

# PKNCA validation: 25(OH)D half-life by BMI z-score group

Table 5 reports the 25(OH)D elimination half-life by BMI z-score group
(medians of the individual estimates). The half-life is computed here with
PKNCA from the dose-attributable concentration (total 25(OH)D minus the
individual baseline) after a single 50,000 IU dose, followed for up to three
years so that the terminal phase is well sampled; dose-attributable
concentrations below 0.01 nmol/L are dropped as below quantification. Time is converted to days
so the half-life is in the paper's unit.

```{r nca}
nca_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~lo, ~hi,
  "Overweight (z 1.00-1.99)", 1.04, 1.99,
  "Obese (z 2.00-2.99)", 2.00, 2.99,
  "Morbidly obese (z >= 3.00)", 3.00, 3.80
)
set.seed(5)
events_nca <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(nca_groups)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  z <- runif(n_per_arm, nca_groups$lo[i], nca_groups$hi[i])
  dose <- tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = 50000 * iu_to_nmol, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = c(0, 1, 3, seq(7, 1092, by = 7)) * 24) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    left_join(tibble(id = ids, BMIZ = z), by = "id") |>
    mutate(group = nca_groups$group[i]) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_nca, keep = c("group", "BMIZ")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  # Dose-attributable 25(OH)D. Below 0.01 nmol/L (1/4000 of the baseline) the
  # difference is ODE-solver noise around a ~40 nmol/L baseline, so those late
  # samples are treated as below quantification. At time 0 the difference
  # is zero up to floating-point rounding, so it is set to exactly 0.
  mutate(
    Cc = Cc - rbase,
    Cc = dplyr::case_when(time == 0 ~ 0, Cc < 0.01 ~ NA_real_, TRUE ~ Cc),
    time = time / 24
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_df <- events_nca |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(time = time / 24) |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~half.life,
  "Overweight (z 1.00-1.99)", 97.7,
  "Obese (z 2.00-2.99)", 65.9,
  "Morbidly obese (z >= 3.00)", 39.1
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "nmol/L", tmax = "day", aucinf.obs = "day*nmol/L", half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (single 50,000 IU dose) vs Table 5 median half-life. * differs from the reference by > 20%.")

hl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(median_hl = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(published, by = "group")
stopifnot(
  # The BMI z-score effect (exponent 0.75 on CL/F, 1 on Vc/F and Q/F) must
  # shorten the half-life from the overweight to the morbidly obese group by
  # well over a third (published 97.7 -> 39.1 days).
  hl$median_hl[hl$group == "Morbidly obese (z >= 3.00)"] <
    0.75 * hl$median_hl[hl$group == "Overweight (z 1.00-1.99)"],
  # Magnitude: each group's median within a factor of 2 of Table 5 (observed
  # while authoring: ratios 1.1, 1.2 and 1.5, the last for the morbidly obese
  # group; see the narrative below).
  all(hl$median_hl / hl$half.life > 0.5 & hl$median_hl / hl$half.life < 2)
)
```

The simulated half-life falls steeply with the BMI z-score, reproducing the
paper's central covariate finding. The simulated group medians sit above the
Table 5 medians, most in the morbidly obese group. Table 5's half-lives are
medians of the 109 children's individual (empirical Bayes) estimates, which
are shrunk towards the typical value and carry each child's actual z-score,
whereas the virtual cohort samples the full population distribution and
spreads z-scores uniformly across each band; the paper itself notes that the
fixed covariate exponents make the half-lives imprecise (Discussion).

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV of the final model.** Table 4 tabulates the final-model IIV as 63%
  (CL/F), 120% (Q/F) and 30% (BASE), consistent with its own bootstrap
  column. The Results text describes these as the values before the BMI
  z-score was added and gives 59%, 104% and 29% after it; the Discussion
  quotes 61%, 96% and 29% for a body-weight model. Because the structural
  estimates of the final model are published only in Table 4, the
  maintainers used the Table 4 IIVs with them. Typical-value predictions are
  unaffected.
- **IIV scale.** The paper reports IIV as %CV for an exponential model.
  The printed RSEs of the IIV terms match the variance-scale RSE of
  CV = sqrt(omega^2) (for example, Part 1 CL/F: printed RSE 62%), so
  omega^2 = CV^2 rather than log(1 + CV^2).
- **Dose unit.** Doses are entered in nmol of vitamin D3 (see Units). The
  paper does not state the unit; the nmol reading is the one that reproduces
  Table 3.
- **Endogenous input.** The paper states that a constant endogenous input to
  the central compartment was used together with the baseline parameter BASE
  but does not print the equation. The model sets the input to CL/F x BASE
  and starts both disposition compartments at BASE, which keeps an undosed
  child at BASE and makes each dose add to it. Individual CL/F and BASE both
  carry IIV, so the input is individual.
- **BMI z-score.** The growth reference is not named. The covariate enters as
  a power of BMIZ / 2.36, so the model needs BMIZ > 0; it was developed in
  children at or above the 85th BMI percentile (z of about 1.04 or more) and
  should not be extrapolated to children of normal weight (Discussion).
- **Virtual cohorts.** The regimen simulations draw from the population
  distribution rather than the 44 Part 1 children's individual estimates
  used by the paper, and the BMI z-score distribution of the final-model
  cohort is assumed (normal, mean 2.36, SD 0.6, truncated to 1.04-3.8).
- **Loading dose timing.** The loading dose is given together with the first
  daily dose at time 0.
- **Not covered.** Table 5's predicted concentrations by z-score group are
  shown for orientation only (see above). No correction notice for the
  article was found as of 2026-11-07.
